what_is_shown: Pilocarpine-induced seizure score over 60 min, three genotypes (image inspected)
groups: pilocarpine vs saline control, per genotype
readout: Modified Racine stage (0-6), mean with SEM, per minute
my_reading: DATO: null reaches stage about 3-4 and stays high; +/+ and +/- plateau near stage 2. INFERENZA: confirms the null is hypersusceptible to a second, mechanistically different convulsant
limit: No drug arm in this panel; n=4 in the null; no statistic printed on the panel

what_is_shown: PTZ and PTZ plus ethosuximide (ETS) over 60 min, wild type (image inspected)
readout: Modified Racine stage, mean with SEM per minute; brackets: *** control v PTZ, n.s. PTZ v PTZ+ETS
my_reading: DATO: PTZ-alone curve peaks near stage 1 to 1.3 at about 10 to 15 min and decays to about 0.3; ETS curve overlaps it (about 0.5 to 0.9 at the peak). INFERENZA: no visible ETS effect, but the whole scale of the response is about 1 stage: a reduction of the size seen in the null (about 1 stage) could not be shown here
limit: Floor: PTZ-alone sits at the bottom of the scale, so a null result is unknown not clean. Unit of the ANOVA (animal or time point) not stated. The text calls the PTZ dose low for this genotype

readout: Modified Racine stage; *** control v PTZ, n.s. PTZ v PTZ+ETS
my_reading: DATO: PTZ and PTZ+ETS both about 0.5 to 1 over the hour and overlapping. INFERENZA: same floor as +/+
limit: Floor; no interaction test; heterozygote is a distinct genotype (reduced Wwox), not a second control

readout: Modified Racine stage; *** control v PTZ and *** PTZ v PTZ+ETS
my_reading: DATO: PTZ-alone about 1.5 to 2.5 in the first 12 min, about 1 to 1.5 for min 15 to 35, rising to about 2 to 2.8 after min 40; PTZ+ETS about 1 to 2 early, about 1.2 mid-hour, about 0.5 to 1 after min 40. INFERENZA: early phase (first 15 min) not visibly different; the separation is in the second half of the hour and rests on the late rise of the PTZ-alone curve
limit: n=6 per arm, graphical reading only (no raw data). The late separation is carried by a PTZ-alone rise that the other null cohort (7d) does not show (see 7d). Statistical unit unstated. Ethosuximide was one pretreatment 45 min before PTZ (Methods); lithium three pretreatments (Methods)

what_is_shown: Western blot of phospho-GSK3B (Ser9), total GSK3B, Wwox and actin in cerebellum, hippocampus and cortex (image inspected; legend: postnatal day 20)
readout: Ratio numbers printed under the lanes
my_reading: DATO: phospho-Ser9 ratio lower in the null in all three regions (printed values about 1.3 v 2.7-3.1 cerebellum, 2.0 v 3.5-3.6 hippocampus, 2.5 v 3.8-3.9 cortex); total GSK3B about 2.2 to 2.6 in all lanes. INFERENZA: GSK3B activation signal in the null at P20; not connected to ethosuximide
limit: Age of the blot (P20) differs from the age of the seizure test (not stated; spontaneous seizures after P12). Single representative blot

what_is_shown: PTZ and PTZ plus LiCl, wild type (image inspected)
readout: Modified Racine stage; **** printed (the legend defines only *** as P<0.001)
my_reading: DATO: PTZ-alone peaks about 1.2 in the first minute and decays to about 0.3; LiCl about 0.2 throughout. INFERENZA: a visible lithium effect at a low baseline, confined to the first minutes
limit: Different cohort and different time profile from 7b +/+ (7b peaks later, about min 10 to 15); **** not defined in the legend; lithium given as three pretreatments within 1 h

my_reading: DATO: PTZ about 0.5 to 1.1; LiCl about 0.1 to 0.4. INFERENZA: lithium effect visible with a low baseline

DATO: PTZ-alone peaks about 3.5 at min 5 to 6, then about 1 to 1.5 for most of the hour; LiCl peaks about 1.3 at min 5 to 8 and is near 0 after about min 20. INFERENZA: lithium acts in the early phase where ethosuximide in 7b did not visibly; the two null PTZ-alone curves (7b v 7d) have different shapes (late rise v early peak), so the two null cohorts are not the same animals and an ETS v lithium ranking across figures is not a head-to-head
limit: No concurrent ETS and LiCl arms; different cohorts; n=6 and 7; the paper states lithium is better than ethosuximide without a direct test
